patch.value: Consume the canonical attestation gate instead of carrying a copy of it

This repository carried its own 721-line shell scanner and 554-line verifier, duplicated from the same origin as every other package in the fleet. That gate decides whether an artefact may reach the registry, so a false pass is the failure that matters - and the canonical implementation has had many fail-open constructions found and closed in it. A copy frozen at any point in that sequence still admits every construction closed after it. The scanner is deleted, the verifier becomes a thin launcher over the published pm-ops/attestation export, and the changelog-date verifier imports its shell helpers from pm-ops/shell-scan. Measured BEFORE: nonliteral-overwrite,nonliteral-overwrite-cmdsub,bare-brace-scope-escape,subshell-scope-escape,cmdsub-in-command-position,backtick-command-position,unset-after-bind,if-branch-bind,semicolon-same-line-bind (9 wrong). Measured AFTER (target): nonliteral-overwrite,nonliteral-overwrite-cmdsub.

Delete scripts/shell-command-scan.ts; Rewrite scripts/verify-release-publish-attestation.ts as a thin launcher over pm-ops/attestation; Repoint scripts/verify-release-changelog-date.ts to pm-ops/shell-scan; Replace test/shell-command-scan.test.ts and test/verify-release-publish-attestation.test.ts as consumer tests; All quality gates pass: check, docstring, coverage, verify:release-publish-attestation, test

value.author: claude
value.text:
Greptile found that the convergence guard did not actually guard. The test asserted that the symbols imported from pm-ops/attestation are functions, and its own comment claimed they were the launcher's functions by reference - but it never compared the two. A launcher that imports the package and then re-exports a local wrapper would have passed, which is exactly the re-fork the test exists to catch.

The test now imports the launcher's own bindings and asserts reference equality against the package's. Proven not vacuous: replacing the re-export with a local arrow wrapper that still calls through to the package makes the test fail, and restoring it makes it pass.

message: review round: the convergence guard did not guard
